title: Reuse already-canonical TensorView entry tuples
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: TensorView construction bounded and froze tensor.entries, then unconditionally called sorted() and tuple() even when the supplied immutable tuple was already in the exact canonical _entry_order. At the declared one-million-entry ceiling, already-canonical producers therefore paid an avoidable full sorting/rematerialization path and transient container overlap despite no ordering work being required.
primary_claim: TensorView now validates entries while tracking whether their existing _entry_order is already nondecreasing. A bounded non-tuple Sequence is frozen once; an exact tuple is reused directly. When the validated entries are already canonical, that tuple becomes the retained TensorView.entries object without a sort/list/final-tuple rematerialization. Unsorted inputs still use the existing deterministic sort, and adjacent duplicate coordinate/relation claims still fail closed after canonicalization.
gardener_decision: Reuse the canonical immutable entry tuple already provided by upstream producers when it satisfies the mandatory order, rather than adding an entry cache/index or always rebuilding the same representation. Keep the legacy deterministic sort only as the fallback for noncanonical input.
acceptance: an exact already-canonical tuple of SparseTensorEntry records is retained by identity after TensorView construction
unsorted entry input remains deterministically canonicalized by the existing _entry_order
duplicate coordinate/relation claims remain fail-closed after canonicalization
bounded-sequence refusal, axis-label lookup and existing construction regressions remain in the focused contract surface
the Fourfold-v2 workflow executes successfully on the exact code/test revision
